The '''2024 World Championship''' was the 29th Star Wars CCG World Championship, held by the [[Players Committee]] at the Zu den Vier Winden bar in Bochum, Germany, over the weekend of 19–22 September 2024.<ref name="wrap" /><ref name="pc">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/2024-09-world-championships-bochum-germany-19-22-september-2024/ 2024-09 World Championships – Bochum, Germany (19-22 September, 2024)], starwarsccg.org</ref> It was the third World Championship held in Europe.<ref name="awards" /> The main event on Saturday had 53 players.<ref name="wrap" /> [[Joe Olson]] defeated [[Emil Wallin]] in the Final Confrontation with Endor Operations and He Is The Chosen One,<ref name="wrap" /><ref name="pc" /> winning his third World Championship and joining [[Bastian Winkelhaus]] and [[Justin Desai]] as three-time champions.<ref name="wrap" /> [[Kevin Jaap]] and [[Hayes Hunter]] were inducted into the Players Committee Hall of Fame during Day 1.<ref name="wrap" /><ref name="awards" />

=== Top 8 bracket ===

After eight Swiss games and four play-in games, [[Timo Dusel]], [[Patrik Csapi]] and Wallin were 7–1; [[Eric Hunter]], Olson, Hayes Hunter and [[Dan Tartaglione]] finished 6–2, in that order; and [[Jonas Hagen Nørregaard]], the best 5–3 player, took the last place in the cut.<ref name="wrap" />
* '''Quarterfinals:''' Olson def. Eric Hunter; Hayes Hunter def. Dusel; Wallin def. Tartaglione; Nørregaard def. Csapi.<ref name="wrap" />
* '''Semifinals:''' Olson def. Hayes Hunter; Wallin def. Nørregaard.<ref name="wrap" />
* '''Final:''' Olson def. Wallin.<ref name="wrap" />

Game scores were not published. The event was not streamed live; recorded games with commentary were posted to the Players Committee YouTube channel.<ref name="wrap" />

== Side events ==

* '''Team tournament''' (Friday evening, glass mug trophies): won by [[Emil Wallin]] and [[Brian Fred]].<ref name="wrap" />
* '''Consolation''' (Sunday, four games, 14 players): won by [[AJ Hatoum]] at 4–0; [[Pär Birgander]] was second.<ref name="wrap" />
* '''Hall of Fame:''' [[Kevin Jaap]] (presented by [[Chris Menzel]] before the main event) and [[Hayes Hunter]] (presented by his brother [[Eric Hunter]] at a mid-day break), both enshrined 21 September 2024.<ref name="wrap" /><ref name="awards" />
* [[Tamás Papp]] was tournament director; Kevin Jaap handled prize support.<ref name="wrap" />
